recognize_zh: 視野中央一顆嗜中性球，細胞核分成約十個以上以細染色質絲相連的小葉，排成環狀（遠超過正常 5 葉的判讀門檻），細胞質為淡粉紅色細顆粒，是巨母紅血球性貧血（megaloblastic anemia）典型的過度分葉嗜中性球。
features: Mature neutrophil with approximately ten nuclear lobes connected by thin chromatin filaments, arranged in a ring
Lobes are small, dense and condensed; cytoplasm shows normal fine pink neutrophilic granulation
Neutrophil diameter slightly exceeds usual size, suggesting a macropolycyte
Background red cells are relatively uniform with mild anisocytosis and a few crenated cells; macro-ovalocytes are not clearly evident in this field
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a markedly hypersegmented neutrophil with approximately ten small nuclear lobes joined by thin chromatin strands and normal cytoplasmic granulation. Surrounding red cells show mild anisocytosis with a few crenated forms; red cell size cannot be reliably judged from this single field and definite macro-ovalocytes are not identified. A single neutrophil with six or more lobes, or more than 5% with five lobes, is significant. Findings are consistent with megaloblastic change, most commonly due to vitamin B12 or folate deficiency, and correlation with MCV, B12, folate and methylmalonic acid is recommended.

ddx.vs: This benign familial trait affects many neutrophils in an otherwise normal smear with normal MCV and vitamin levels.
Morphology is identical; medication history and normal B12/folate levels separate it.
MDS more often shows hypolobated (pseudo-Pelger) and hypogranular neutrophils with cytopenias rather than prominent hypersegmentation.

ddx.dx: Iron deficiency or renal failure related hypersegmentation
ddx.vs: These show only mild hypersegmentation (5-6 lobes) with microcytic or normocytic red cells, not ten-lobed neutrophils.
